react:
With the classic JSX runtime, what does
Hi
compile to?
React.createElement("div", { className: "box" }, "Hi")
document.createElement("div") with className set to "box"
A template string assigned to innerHTML at runtime
React.render("div", { className: "box" }, "Hi")
JSX is syntax sugar: the classic transform turns each element into a React.createElement call that returns a plain object describing the UI.
Why must a custom component such as <UserCard /> start with a capital letter in JSX?
Lowercase tags are treated as built-in HTML elements
Lowercase names are reserved for class components
Capital letters make the component render faster
React Hooks only work inside files with capitalized names
JSX treats <usercard /> as the string tag "usercard" passed to the DOM, while <UserCard /> refers to the variable UserCard.

In React, what does {0 &&

Empty

} render?
The text 0
Nothing at all
Empty
The text false
&& returns the left operand when it is falsy. React skips false, null and undefined, but it renders numbers, so 0 appears on the page. Use count > 0 && ... instead.
Which hook keeps a mutable value across renders without causing a re-render when it changes?
useRef
useState
useReducer
useContext
Changing ref.current does not schedule a render. useState and useReducer updates do trigger re-renders.
A click handler runs setCount(count + 1) three times in a row, with count starting at 0. What is count after one click?
All three calls read the same count value (0) from the current render, so each one schedules 0 + 1.
A handler should add 3 to count by calling the state setter three times. Which change makes it work?
Use the updater form setCount(c => c + 1) for each call
Call setCount(count + 1) inside a setTimeout for each call
Store count in a plain let variable and increment it three times
Wrap the three setCount(count + 1) calls in a useMemo hook
The updater function receives the latest pending state, so the three updates chain to 3. Since React 18, updates inside setTimeout are batched too, so that does not help.
Outside of Strict Mode, when does the effect in useEffect(fn, []) run?
Once, after the component first mounts
Before every render of the component
After every render of the component
Only when the component unmounts
An empty dependency array means the effect has no dependencies that can change, so it runs once after mount. In Strict Mode development React runs it twice to surface missing cleanups.
When does the cleanup function returned from a useEffect callback run?
Before the effect re-runs and when the component unmounts
Only once, right after the first render of the component
Before every render, even if the dependencies are unchanged
Only when the page is reloaded or the browser tab is closed
React runs the previous cleanup before running the effect again with new dependencies, and once more on unmount.
Which statement about useCallback(fn, deps) is accurate?
It is equivalent to useMemo(() => fn, deps)
It runs fn immediately and caches its result
It makes fn run in a background thread
It prevents the component from re-rendering
useCallback memoizes the function itself, while useMemo memoizes the value returned by calling a function. Neither one stops the component from rendering.
This effect runs once: useEffect(() => { const id = setInterval(() => setCount(count + 1), 1000); return () => clearInterval(id); }, []). What happens to count (starting at 0)?
It becomes 1 and then stays at 1
It increases by 1 every second
It increases by 2 every second
React throws a missing dependency error
The interval callback closes over count from the first render (0), so it keeps setting 1. Using setCount(c => c + 1) fixes the stale closure.
What is the virtual DOM in React?
An in-memory tree of elements React compares to find DOM changes
A browser API that renders whole pages off-screen to make them faster
The Shadow DOM that isolates each component's styles
A copy of the rendered page that is stored on the server
React builds lightweight element objects, diffs the new tree against the previous one, and applies only the needed changes to the real DOM.
Why is using the array index as key risky for a list where items can be inserted or reordered?
Component state can stay attached to the wrong item
React refuses to render lists keyed by numbers
Index keys disable batching of state updates
The list is re-sorted alphabetically by React
Keys tell React which item is which. When indexes shift, React matches old state (such as input text) to a different item. Use a stable id instead.

During reconciliation, a parent switches from rendering
to
. What happens to Form's state?
It is lost, because the subtree is unmounted and remounted
It is kept, because Form is the same component
It is kept, but Form's effects do not re-run
React throws an error about changing element types at runtime
When the element type at a position changes, React destroys the old subtree and builds a new one, so all state inside it resets.
A component renders {isAdmin ? <Counter label="a" /> : <Counter label="b" />}. When isAdmin toggles, what happens to Counter's internal state?
It is preserved, as the same type is at the same spot
It resets, because the JSX lives in two separate branches
It resets, because the label prop changed between renders
It is moved into the parent and restored on the next render
React tracks state by component type and position in the tree. Adding a different key to each branch would force a reset.
Two sibling components must show and edit the same value. What is the standard React approach?
Lift the state into their closest common parent
Copy the state into both siblings and sync with useEffect
Store the value in a global variable outside React
Let one sibling read the other's state through a ref
Lifting state up gives a single source of truth: the parent owns the value and passes it, plus an update callback, down as props.
A component calls useContext(ThemeContext), but no matching provider exists above it. What does it receive?
The default value passed to createContext
undefined, plus a console warning
An error thrown during rendering
The value from the nearest sibling provider
useContext looks for the closest provider above the component. If none exists, it returns the default value given to createContext(defaultValue).
A provider uses value={{ user, setUser }}, and all consumers re-render whenever the provider's parent re-renders. Which fix fits best?
Memoize the object with useMemo, keyed on user
Switch the consumers to class components
Replace useContext with a direct import
Wrap each consumer's output in a Fragment
An object literal creates a new reference every render, so React sees a changed context value. useMemo keeps the same object until user changes.
What does wrapping a component in React.memo do?
Skips re-rendering when its props are shallowly equal
Caches the component's DOM nodes in localStorage
Prevents the component's own state from changing
Renders the component only once for the whole lifetime of the app
React.memo compares previous and next props with Object.is per prop. State or context changes inside the component still trigger renders.
Which of these is not allowed inside a React Server Component?
Calling useState
Awaiting a database query
Rendering a Client Component
Reading a file on the server
Server Components run only on the server and have no interactivity, so state and effect hooks are unavailable. They can be async and can render Client Components.
What does the "use client" directive at the top of a file do in a React Server Components setup?
Marks the file as a boundary whose components run on the client
Makes the components in the file render only after the user clicks
Disables server-side HTML rendering for the whole application
Imports React DOM automatically into the file and its children
"use client" marks a module, and everything it imports, as part of the client bundle. Client Components are still pre-rendered to HTML on the server in frameworks like Next.js.
nextjs: In the Next.js App Router, which file makes the route /dashboard publicly accessible?
app/dashboard/page.tsx
app/dashboard/index.tsx
app/dashboard/route-ui.tsx
app/dashboard/layout.tsx
A route segment becomes reachable only when it has a page file. A layout wraps pages but does not create a route on its own.
In the Next.js Pages Router, when does getServerSideProps run?
On the server, for every request to that page
On the server, once at build time for each page
In the browser, right after hydration
Only when the page is revalidated
getServerSideProps runs on each request on the server and passes its result as props. getStaticProps is the build-time variant.
In the Pages Router, getStaticProps returns { props, revalidate: 60 }. What does this enable?
Incremental Static Regeneration every 60 seconds at most
Server-side rendering on every single request
A full rebuild of the whole site every 60 seconds
Client-side refetching of the page props every 60 seconds
With revalidate, Next.js serves the static page and regenerates it in the background on a request after the 60-second window expires.
Which App Router pattern replaces getServerSideProps for fetching data?
Fetching data directly inside an async Server Component
Exporting getServerSideProps from page.tsx
Calling fetch inside a useEffect hook in the root layout.tsx
Adding a getInitialProps method to the page
In the App Router, Server Components can be async and await data directly. The Pages Router data functions are not supported in the app directory.
In the App Router, how do you statically generate pages for a dynamic segment such as app/blog/[slug]/page.tsx?
Export generateStaticParams from the page
Export getStaticPaths from the page
Add the slugs to next.config.js routes
Create one folder for every slug by hand
generateStaticParams returns the list of params to pre-render at build time. getStaticPaths is the Pages Router equivalent.
In the Next.js App Router, what kind of component is a file in the app directory by default?
A Server Component
A Client Component
A static HTML template
An API Route handler
Components in app are Server Components unless the file, or a module importing it, starts with "use client".
A component in the app directory calls useState and fails to build. What is the usual fix?
Add "use client" at the top of that component's file
Rename the file from page.tsx to page.jsx
Move the component into the public folder
Wrap the component in a Suspense boundary in its layout
Hooks such as useState need a Client Component. The "use client" directive marks the file as running in the browser too.
A Server Component renders <Button onClick={() => console.log("x")} />, where Button is a Client Component. What happens?
An error, as functions cannot be passed to Client Components
The function is serialized with the props and runs in the browser
The click handler runs on the server whenever clicked
The prop is dropped silently, with no message at all
Props crossing from server to client must be serializable. Plain functions are not; only Server Actions are a special exception.
Which file handles GET requests to /api/hello in the App Router?
app/api/hello/route.ts exporting a GET function
app/api/hello/page.ts exporting a default handler
pages/api/hello/route.ts exporting a GET function
app/api/hello/handler.ts exporting get()
Route Handlers live in route.ts (or .js) files and export functions named after HTTP methods, such as GET and POST.
What happens if app/blog/route.ts and app/blog/page.tsx both exist?
Next.js reports a conflict for that route segment
The page handles GET and the route handles POST
The route handler silently overrides the page
The page always wins and route.ts is ignored
A route segment can have either a page or a route handler at the same level, not both.
In Next.js 13 to 15, where must the middleware file live?
middleware.ts at the project root, or in src
app/middleware/page.ts inside the app folder
pages/_middleware.ts placed in every folder
public/middleware.js next to static assets
Next.js looks for a single middleware file at the root (next to app or pages, or in src). Next.js 16 renamed this convention to proxy.ts.
In Next.js 13 to 15 middleware, which config limits it to /dashboard and its subpaths?
export const config = { matcher: "/dashboard/:path*" }
export const routes = ["/dashboard"]
export const config = { include: "/dashboard" }
export const matcher = { path: "dashboard/**" }
The exported config.matcher filters which paths run the middleware; :path* matches zero or more segments.
Inside Next.js middleware (versions 13 to 15), which code redirects the user to /login?
return NextResponse.redirect(new URL("/login", request.url))
return res.redirect(302, "/login") like in Express
window.location.href = "/login" inside the function
router.push("/login") using useRouter from next/navigation
Middleware runs on the server before the route, so there is no window or router. NextResponse.redirect needs an absolute URL, built here from request.url.
Besides alt, which props must next/image receive for a remote URL string as src when fill is not used?
width and height
loader and quality
priority and sizes
placeholder and blurDataURL
Next.js needs the intrinsic size of a remote image to reserve space and avoid layout shift. Static imports provide it automatically.
next/image throws an error for a URL on images.example.com. What usually fixes it?
Allow that host in images.remotePatterns
Add crossOrigin="anonymous" to the Image component
Move the image file into the app directory
Set unoptimized: false on the Image component
The image optimizer only processes remote hosts you allow, to prevent abuse. remotePatterns lists the allowed protocols, hosts and paths.
By default, how does next/image load an image that is far below the fold?
Lazily, as it nears the viewport
Eagerly, together with the page HTML
Only after the user clicks on it
As a data URI inlined in the HTML
next/image uses native lazy loading by default. Above-the-fold images such as a hero should be marked to load eagerly.
In a Client Component, a chart library accesses window at import time and crashes during server rendering. Which fix fits?
const Chart = dynamic(() => import("./Chart"), { ssr: false })
const Chart = await import("./Chart") at the top level of the file
Wrap the import statement in a try/catch block in the file
Rename the file to Chart.client.tsx so it skips the server
next/dynamic with ssr: false skips server rendering for that component and loads it only in the browser.
What does next/dynamic(() => import("./HeavyEditor")) do for bundle size?
Splits HeavyEditor into a chunk loaded when it renders
Inlines HeavyEditor into the main bundle for faster loads
Removes HeavyEditor from production builds entirely
Moves HeavyEditor into a Web Worker thread at runtime
Dynamic imports create a separate JavaScript chunk, so pages that never render the component do not download its code.
When a user navigates from /dashboard/a to /dashboard/b, how does app/dashboard/layout.tsx behave?
It stays mounted and keeps its state
It unmounts and remounts with fresh state
It reloads the whole page from the server
It renders twice, once for each route
Layouts are shared across the routes below them and persist during navigation; only the changed page segment re-renders.
What does adding loading.tsx to an App Router segment do?
Shows its UI as a Suspense fallback while the page loads
Preloads every link on the page in the background
Shows a spinner only on full browser page reloads
Delays navigation until all images have loaded
Next.js wraps the segment's page in a React Suspense boundary with loading.tsx as the fallback, enabling instant loading states.
vue: In Vue 3, given const count = ref(0), how do you increment it inside <script setup>?
count.value++
count += 1
count.set(count + 1)
this.count++
A ref wraps the value in an object with a .value property. Templates unwrap refs automatically, but script code must use .value.
In Vue 3, const { count } = reactive({ count: 0 }). Is count still reactive?
No, it copies a plain value; toRefs keeps reactivity
Yes, reactive() turns every property into a ref
Yes, but only when count is used inside the template
No, and reactive() objects cannot be destructured
reactive() tracks property access on the proxy. Destructuring reads the value once, so the local variable is disconnected from the source.
In Vue 3, you run state.extra = 1 on an object created with reactive({}). What happens?
The new property is reactive, thanks to Proxy
Nothing updates until you call Vue.set on it
Vue throws an error about the unknown key
Only the template sees it, watchers do not
Vue 3's Proxy-based system intercepts property additions. Vue 2 used getters and setters and needed Vue.set for new properties.
What distinguishes computed() from a method in Vue?
computed caches its result until reactive dependencies change
computed reruns on every render, while methods cache their result
computed can only return strings, never objects or arrays
computed runs only on the server, during SSR rendering
A computed value re-evaluates only when something it read changes; a method called in a template runs again on every render.
How does watchEffect differ from watch in Vue 3?
It runs at once and tracks what it reads automatically
It needs an explicit list of reactive sources to watch
It runs only once, when the component is unmounted
It passes both the old and new values to its callback
watchEffect runs immediately and re-runs when any reactive value it touched changes. watch takes explicit sources, is lazy by default and provides old and new values.
In a Vue 3 single-file component using <script setup>, how does a top-level const become usable in the template?
It is available in the template automatically
It must be returned from a setup() function
It must be listed in the components option
It must be registered with app.provide()
With <script setup>, top-level bindings (variables, functions, imports) are exposed to the template with no return statement.
In the Options API, why must data be written as a function, as in data() { return { n: 0 } }?
So each instance gets its own fresh state object
So Vue can evaluate data on the server only
So the data can be loaded lazily from an API
So templates can call data like a normal method
If data were a shared object, every instance would mutate the same state. Returning a new object per call isolates instances.
In the Options API, how does a method read a value defined in data?
Through this, as in this.items
Through props.items directly
Through a data.items variable
Through the $data().items call
Vue proxies data properties onto the component instance, so methods, computed properties and watchers access them via this.
A Vue template shows {{ html }} where html is "Hi". What appears on the page?
The literal text Hi
The word Hi in bold text
Nothing, the tags are stripped
A Vue compilation error
Mustache interpolation escapes HTML. v-html renders raw HTML, but only use it with trusted content because of XSS risk.
In Vue templates, what are the shorthands for v-bind:href and v-on:click?
:href and @click
#href and :click
@href and #click
$href and &click
The colon is shorthand for v-bind and the at sign for v-on. The hash is shorthand for v-slot.
How does v-show differ from v-if when the condition is false?
v-show keeps the element in the DOM and sets display: none
v-show removes the element from the DOM and destroys its state
v-show only works on components, not elements
v-show evaluates its condition just once
v-if conditionally renders the element, while v-show only toggles CSS display, which is cheaper for frequent toggling.
In Vue 3, an element has v-for="u in users" and v-if="u.active" together. What happens?
v-if is evaluated first, so u is not defined yet
Only active users are rendered, exactly as intended
v-for runs first and filters the list
Vue renders all users and ignores v-if
In Vue 3, v-if has higher priority than v-for on the same element. Filter with a computed list or put v-for on a wrapping <template>.
In Vue 3, v-model="title" on a custom component expands to which prop and event?
modelValue and update:modelValue
value and update:value
modelValue and change:modelValue
title and update:title
Vue 3 changed the defaults from Vue 2's value and input. The component must accept modelValue and emit update:modelValue.
What does the .lazy modifier change in <input v-model.lazy="name">?
It syncs on the change event instead of every input event
It loads the input element only when it scrolls into view
It trims leading and trailing whitespace from the value
It converts the typed value to a number before syncing
By default v-model syncs on input. .lazy syncs on change, such as when the field loses focus. .trim and .number are other modifiers.
In Vue Router 4, how does a component read the id from the route /users/:id?
useRoute().params.id
useRouter().params.id
this.$params.id
window.location.id
useRoute returns the current route object, including params and query. useRouter returns the router instance used for navigation.
In Vue Router 4, a global router.beforeEach guard returns false. What happens?
The current navigation is cancelled
The app reloads at the root URL
The guard is skipped and navigation proceeds
The router throws an uncaught error
Returning false aborts navigation. Returning a route location, such as { name: "login" }, redirects instead.
With createWebHistory, refreshing /users/5 on a static host returns 404. What is the cause?
The server has no fallback to index.html for that path
Vue Router does not support numeric route params like /users/5
The route was registered after app.mount() ran
History mode only works on the dev server
In HTML5 history mode the browser requests the real path from the server. Configure a fallback to index.html, or use hash mode.
In a Pinia store component, const { count } = useCounterStore() stops updating. Which fix keeps reactivity?
Destructure with storeToRefs(store)
Destructure with Object.assign(store)
Call store.$reset() before destructuring
Wrap the store in JSON.parse(JSON.stringify())
A store is a reactive object, so plain destructuring copies values. storeToRefs creates refs for state and getters; actions can be destructured directly.
In a Pinia store defined with the options syntax, what are getters equivalent to?
Computed values derived from the state
Async functions that call APIs
Watchers that run on every change
Mutations that commit state changes
Pinia getters are cached computed values based on state. Actions hold logic and can be async.
Compared to Vuex, which statement about Pinia is accurate?
Actions can change state directly, with no mutations
State can only change through mutations committed by actions
Stores must all be nested inside a single root module
It works only with the Options API, not with setup()
Pinia dropped mutations: actions, or even components, modify state directly while devtools still track changes. It supports both APIs.
nuxt: In Nuxt 3 with default settings, how is a page rendered on the first visit?
HTML is rendered on the server, then hydrated in the browser
The browser receives an empty shell and renders everything
Every page is prerendered at build time only
The server streams JSON and the client builds HTML
Nuxt's default universal rendering sends server-rendered HTML for fast first paint and SEO, then hydrates it so it becomes interactive.
How do you turn off server-side rendering for an entire Nuxt 3 app?
Set ssr: false in nuxt.config
Delete the server directory
Add <ClientOnly> around app.vue
Set target: "static" in package.json
ssr: false makes Nuxt render as a single-page app on the client. ClientOnly only affects the components inside it.
Which Nuxt 3 config renders /admin/** only on the client while other routes keep SSR?
routeRules: { "/admin/**": { ssr: false } }
ssr: { exclude: ["/admin/**"], mode: "spa" }
pages: { "/admin/**": { mode: "client" } }
nitro: { routes: { "/admin/**": "spa" } }
routeRules enables hybrid rendering, so each route pattern can choose SSR, client-only, prerendering or caching rules.
Which file creates the route /users/:id in Nuxt 3?
pages/users/[id].vue
pages/users/:id.vue
pages/users/{id}.vue
routes/users/id.vue
Square brackets mark a dynamic segment in Nuxt's file-based routing; the value is read with useRoute().params.id.
Which file in pages/ matches any path, such as /docs/a/b/c, in Nuxt 3?
pages/[...slug].vue
pages/[slug].vue
pages/*.vue
pages/_all.vue
The spread syntax creates a catch-all route; slug becomes an array of the path segments.
A Nuxt 3 app has a pages directory, but nothing from it shows up. What is likely missing from app.vue?
The <NuxtPage /> component
The <RouterView name="pages" /> tag
An import of every page file
A routes array exported from app.vue
When app.vue exists, it is the root component and must render <NuxtPage /> where the current page should appear.
Nuxt has pages/parent.vue and pages/parent/child.vue. What must parent.vue contain for /parent/child to show the child?
A <NuxtPage /> component where the child renders
A <slot name="child" /> element where it renders
An import of child.vue at the top of its script
A children array listed in definePageMeta
A file next to a folder of the same name becomes a parent route, and nested pages render in its <NuxtPage />.
In Nuxt 3, how do you use components/base/Button.vue in a template with default auto-imports?
<BaseButton />
<Button from="base" />
<base-button-vue />
<Base.Button />
Nuxt auto-imports components and prefixes the name with nested directory names, so base/Button.vue becomes BaseButton.
In Nuxt 3, which code is auto-imported by default with no import statement?
Top-level files in composables/ and Vue APIs like ref
Every .ts file anywhere in the project folder tree
Only files whose names start with the use prefix
Nothing, Nuxt requires explicit import statements everywhere
Nuxt scans composables/ and utils/ at the top level, and auto-imports Vue APIs and Nuxt composables like useFetch. Nested composable folders are not scanned by default.
Which file makes the endpoint /api/hello in Nuxt 3?
server/api/hello.ts exporting defineEventHandler
pages/api/hello.vue with a <server> block inside
api/hello.ts at the root exporting a GET function
server/hello.api.ts exporting a handler() function
Files in server/api are registered under /api, and each one default-exports a handler created with defineEventHandler.
In Nuxt 3, how does server/routes/sitemap.xml.ts differ from server/api/sitemap.xml.ts?
server/routes adds no /api prefix: it serves /sitemap.xml
server/routes files only run once, at build time
server/routes files are rendered as client-side pages
There is no difference, both serve /api/sitemap.xml
Both directories become server endpoints, but only server/api prefixes paths with /api.
What is Nitro in Nuxt 3?
The server engine that builds for many deploy targets
The Vue compiler that turns templates into JavaScript
The state manager that replaced Vuex in Nuxt 3
The CSS engine that bundles and purges all styles
Nitro powers the server directory and produces output for presets like Node.js, serverless platforms and edge runtimes.
Inside a Nuxt 3 POST event handler, how do you read the JSON body?
const body = await readBody(event)
const body = event.body.json()
const body = useState("body")
const body = await fetch(event).json()
readBody comes from h3, the HTTP framework under Nitro, and is auto-imported in the server directory. getQuery reads query parameters.
Which Nuxt 3 composable sets meta tags with a flat, typed API, such as ogTitle and description?
useSeoMeta
useMetaTags
definePageMeta
useOpenGraph
useSeoMeta takes flat keys and outputs the matching meta tags. definePageMeta sets route metadata such as layout and middleware, not head tags.
Where can you set default <head> tags that apply to every page in a Nuxt 3 app?
app.head in nuxt.config
head.config.ts in the root
The <head> of public/index.html
nitro.head in nuxt.config
app.head defines global title, meta and link defaults. Pages can override them with useHead or useSeoMeta.
In a Nuxt SEO setup, which module generates a sitemap.xml from your routes?
@nuxtjs/sitemap
@nuxtjs/router-map
@nuxt/xml
@nuxtjs/head
@nuxtjs/sitemap is part of the Nuxt SEO module family, alongside modules such as @nuxtjs/robots.
Why does useAsyncData("posts", () => $fetch("/api/posts")) take a key such as "posts"?
To dedupe requests and reuse server data during hydration
To name the server API route that Nuxt should generate for it
To encrypt the data on its way from server to client
To store the result in localStorage under that key
Data fetched during SSR is sent to the client in the payload under that key, so the client reuses it instead of fetching again.
Why should you avoid calling $fetch directly at the top of a page's setup in Nuxt 3?
It runs on the server and again in the browser
$fetch is not available inside page components
$fetch only works for external third-party URLs
$fetch cannot parse JSON responses by itself
Without useAsyncData or useFetch, nothing transfers the server result to the client, so the request is made twice.
How is useFetch("/api/posts") related to useAsyncData in Nuxt 3?
It is a shortcut for useAsyncData with $fetch
It is an older API that useAsyncData replaced
It only runs in the browser, never on the server
It returns a plain Promise with no refs
useFetch builds a key from the URL and calls useAsyncData with $fetch, returning the same data, status, error and refresh values.
Which useAsyncData option makes the fetch run only in the browser, skipping SSR?
server: false
client: true
ssr: "skip"
immediate: false
With server: false the data loads after hydration. lazy: true keeps SSR but does not block navigation; immediate: false delays the first call.
svelte: What is the main idea behind Svelte's compile-time reactivity?
Components compile into JS that updates the DOM directly
A virtual DOM is diffed in the browser on each change
The browser interprets .svelte files at runtime
A server re-renders HTML after every state change
The Svelte compiler analyzes components at build time and generates code that updates exactly the affected DOM nodes, with no virtual DOM diffing.
In Svelte 4, a component has let items = [1, 2] and runs items.push(3). Why does the UI not update?
Svelte 4 reacts to assignments, not to mutations
Arrays can never be reactive in Svelte components
push is blocked inside Svelte components at runtime
The UI updates only after a full page reload
Svelte 4 instruments assignments. Write items = [...items, 3], or add items = items after the push.
In Svelte 4, let obj = { a: 1 }; const o = obj; o.a = 2. Does markup that shows {obj.a} update?
No, because the assignment targets o, not obj
Yes, because both names point to one object
Yes, but only after a tick() call
No, because objects cannot be reactive
Svelte 4 triggers updates when the updated variable's name appears on the left side of an assignment. Assigning through another reference is not tracked.
In Svelte 4, what does $: doubled = count * 2 do?
Recomputes doubled whenever count changes
Computes doubled once at component creation
Declares doubled as a two-way bound prop
Creates a store named doubled
$: marks a reactive declaration. Svelte re-runs it when any variable it references changes.
In Svelte 4, which reactive statement logs every time count changes?
$: console.log(count)
$: console.log()
on:count={console.log}
$console.log(count)
Svelte re-runs a $: statement when variables referenced in it change. With no reference to count, it would not depend on count.
In Svelte 4, with $: total = a + b, what happens when only b changes?
total is recalculated, since it depends on a and b
total stays the same until a also changes
Svelte throws an error about stale values
total is recalculated only on the next mount
A reactive declaration depends on every variable referenced in it, so a change to either a or b re-runs it before the DOM updates.
In a Svelte component, what does $count mean when count is a writable store?
It subscribes to the store and unsubscribes on destroy
It reads the store value only once, at mount time
It creates a new store copied from the count store
It marks count as a reactive declaration like $:
Prefixing a store with $ inside a component subscribes to it and cleans up automatically. Assigning to $count calls set as well.
Which call increments a Svelte writable store named count by 1?
count.update(n => n + 1)
count.set(count + 1)
count.value += 1
count.subscribe(n => n + 1)
update takes a function of the current value. count itself is the store object, so count + 1 does not produce a number.
Which svelte/store function creates a store whose value is computed from other stores?
derived
readable
computed
writable
derived(source, fn) recalculates its value when the source stores change. readable is for values set only from inside the store.
Outside a component, how do you read the current value of a Svelte store just once?
get(store) from svelte/store
store.value, read directly
store.current() from svelte/store
$store in a plain .js file
get subscribes, reads the value and unsubscribes immediately. The $ prefix only works inside components.
In Svelte, when does an onMount callback run?
After the component is first rendered to the DOM
Before the component's script block runs at all
Every time any reactive state in it changes
During server-side rendering only, never in the browser
onMount runs once in the browser after the initial render. If it returns a function, that function runs when the component is destroyed.
Why is onMount a safe place in SvelteKit to access window or document?
onMount does not run during server-side rendering
onMount runs before the server sends HTML
SvelteKit polyfills window on the server
onMount runs inside a Web Worker that mocks the DOM
Lifecycle functions other than onDestroy do not run on the server. Code that needs browser APIs belongs in onMount.
In Svelte, what does await tick() do?
Waits until pending state changes reach the DOM
Pauses the component for exactly one second
Forces the component to fully unmount and remount
Waits for the next network request to finish
Svelte batches updates. tick returns a promise that resolves once the DOM reflects the latest state.
In Svelte 4, how does a parent fill a named slot declared as <slot name="header" /> in a Card component?
Title
<Card:header>Title</Card:header>
<template #header>Title</template>
An element with slot="header", placed inside <Card>, goes to the matching named slot. The #header syntax is Vue; Svelte 5 replaces slots with snippets.
In Svelte 4, a Button has <slot>Click me</slot>. What renders for <Button />, with no content?
The fallback text Click me
An empty button element
The text undefined as a label
A compile error about a missing slot
Content inside a <slot> element is fallback content, shown only when the parent provides nothing for that slot.
In Svelte, how does in:fly differ from transition:fly on an element?
in:fly plays only when the element enters the DOM
in:fly plays only when the element leaves the DOM
in:fly plays on every state change
in:fly can only be used on components
transition: runs on both enter and leave. in: and out: apply a transition to one direction only.
Which Svelte directive animates items smoothly into new positions when a keyed each block is reordered?
animate:flip
transition:slide
in:reorder
use:move
animate:flip from svelte/animate uses the FLIP technique. It only works on direct children of a keyed {#each} block.
In SvelteKit, which file defines the page for the route /about?
src/routes/about/+page.svelte
src/pages/about/+page.svelte
src/routes/about/page.svelte
src/routes/+about.svelte
SvelteKit uses folders for routes and the +page.svelte file for the page component in each folder.
In SvelteKit, a load function uses a database password. Where should it be placed?
In +page.server.js, so it runs only on the server
In +page.js, which SvelteKit runs only on the server
In +page.svelte, inside an onMount callback
In +layout.svelte, inside a script tag
+page.server.js load functions never run in the browser. Universal +page.js load functions can run on both server and client.
In SvelteKit, where do form actions that handle a POST from a <form method="POST"> live?
In an actions export in +page.server.js
In a submit handler in +layout.js
In a POST export from +page.svelte
In hooks.client.js, in a handleSubmit export
Form actions are exported as actions from +page.server.js and run on the server. They work even without JavaScript in the browser.
angular: In an NgModule-based Angular app, what belongs in the declarations array?
Components, directives and pipes it owns
Services that the module provides app-wide
Other modules that this module imports
Routes that the module defines for lazy loading
declarations lists non-standalone declarables. Services go in providers, and other modules go in imports.
A standalone Angular component uses the async pipe in its template. Where do you make the pipe available?
In the component's own imports array
In a declarations array on the component
In the providers array of main.ts
Nowhere, pipes are always global
Standalone components declare their template dependencies in imports, such as AsyncPipe, CommonModule or other standalone components.
Which function starts an Angular app whose root component is standalone?
bootstrapApplication(AppComponent, appConfig)
platformBrowserDynamic().bootstrapModule(AppComponent)
createApp(AppComponent).mount("#app")
new AppComponent().bootstrap(appConfig)
bootstrapApplication is the standalone entry point. bootstrapModule bootstraps an NgModule, not a component.
What does @Injectable({ providedIn: "root" }) on a service do?
Registers one app-wide instance that can be tree-shaken
Creates a new instance for every component that injects it
Makes the service available only inside AppModule
Injects the service into every component automatically
providedIn root registers the service with the root injector as a singleton. If nothing injects it, the build can remove it.
A service is listed in a component's providers array. What does that give you?
A separate service instance per component instance
One instance shared by the whole application
An instance that is created only on the server
A compile error, since services need an NgModule
Component-level providers create an element injector, so each component instance (and its children) gets its own copy.
Where can you call inject(HttpClient) in an Angular component class?
In a field initializer or the constructor
Inside a setTimeout callback in ngOnInit
Inside a click handler method
Inside a promise.then in ngAfterViewInit
inject only works in an injection context, such as construction time. Calling it later in callbacks throws an error.
An Angular component calls this.http.get("/api/users") and never subscribes. What happens?
No HTTP request is sent at all
The request is sent and the result is cached
The request is sent and the result discarded
Angular subscribes automatically after a delay
HttpClient returns a cold Observable. The request starts only when something subscribes, for example the async pipe.
For a search box that calls an API on each keystroke, which RxJS operator drops results of outdated requests?
switchMap
mergeMap
concatMap
map
switchMap unsubscribes from the previous inner Observable when a new value arrives, which cancels the stale HTTP request. mergeMap keeps them all.
How does a BehaviorSubject differ from a plain Subject in RxJS?
It needs an initial value and gives new subscribers the latest one
It emits values only once and then completes immediately
It can only be subscribed to a single time, then it errors
It runs all of its subscribers on a separate background worker thread
A late subscriber to a Subject misses earlier values. A BehaviorSubject immediately emits its current value on subscribe.
What does {{ user$ | async }} do in an Angular template?
Subscribes to user$ and unsubscribes on destroy
Converts user$ into a Promise and reads it once
Delays all rendering until the user has logged in
Runs user$ on the server before the page renders
The async pipe manages the subscription lifecycle and marks the view for check whenever a new value arrives.
In Angular, what does the @Input() decorator on a property do?
Lets a parent bind a value to it in the template
Reads a value from an HTML form field on the page
Injects a service into the property at runtime
Emits an event up to the parent component
@Input marks a property that a parent sets with property binding, such as [title]="x". @Output with EventEmitter sends events up.
In Angular, a component has selector: "app-card". How is it used in another template?
<app-card></app-card>
<div component="app-card" />
<AppCard></AppCard>
<app-card-component />
The selector tells Angular where to create the component. An element selector like app-card matches the custom tag.
Which decorator makes a method run when the browser window is resized?
@HostListener("window:resize", ["$event"])
@Output("window:resize", ["$event"])
@ViewChild("window:resize", ["$event"])
@HostBinding("window:resize", ["$event"])
@HostListener subscribes a method to events on the host element or on global targets such as window and document.
A pure Angular pipe filters an array, and the view does not update after this.items.push(x). Why?
Pure pipes re-run only for a new input reference
Pipes cannot receive arrays as their input value
push calls are blocked by Angular zones
Pure pipes run only once for the whole app
Angular skips a pure pipe if its inputs are the same references. Assign a new array, such as this.items = [...this.items, x].
With the default en-US locale, what does {{ 1234.5 | currency:"USD" }} output?
CurrencyPipe uses the locale's format: a symbol, grouping separators and two decimal places for USD.
In Angular, how does a structural directive such as *ngIf differ from an attribute directive such as ngClass?
Structural directives add or remove elements from the DOM
Structural directives only change CSS classes
Structural directives can only be used on components, not elements
Structural directives run only on the server
Structural directives shape the DOM by creating or destroying views. Attribute directives change the look or behavior of an existing element.
A route is { path: "user/:id", component: UserComponent }. How does UserComponent read the id with ActivatedRoute?
From route.paramMap, using get("id")
From route.queryParams.id only
From window.history.state.id
From the component's selector
Path parameters are available on ActivatedRoute.paramMap (or snapshot.paramMap). queryParams holds the ?key=value part.
A functional CanActivateFn should send unauthenticated users to /login. What should it return for them?
router.createUrlTree(["/login"])
window.location.assign("/login")
a new Error("/login") object
the string "redirect:/login"
Returning a UrlTree from a guard cancels the current navigation and starts one to that URL. Returning false only cancels.
Which route config lazy-loads a standalone AdminComponent in Angular?
loadComponent: () => import("./admin").then(m => m.AdminComponent)
component: import("./admin").then(m => m.AdminComponent)
lazy: "./admin#AdminComponent" inside the route object
loadChildren: AdminComponent with no import function
loadComponent takes a function returning a dynamic import, so the component code is split into its own chunk and loaded on first visit.
In Angular, const a = signal(2); const b = computed(() => a() * 10); a.set(3). What does b() return?
undefined
It throws
computed tracks the signals it reads. After a changes, the next read of b recomputes using the new value 3.
html: Which element should wrap the dominant, unique content of a page, excluding headers, footers and sidebars?
<main>
<section>
<body>
<article>
<main> marks the primary content and should appear once per page (only one visible at a time). It also gives assistive tech a landmark to jump to.
Which element suits a blog post that could be syndicated or reused on its own?
<article>
<section>
<aside>
<div>
<article> is for self-contained content. <section> groups related content under a heading but is not meant to stand alone.
Why is <button> preferred over <div onclick="..."> for a clickable control?
It is focusable and works with the keyboard by default
It loads faster than a div in every modern browser
It is the only element that accepts an onclick handler
It blocks the click event from bubbling up the DOM
Native buttons get focus, Enter and Space activation and the button role for free. A div needs all of that added by hand.
An icon-only button shows a magnifier SVG and no text. How do you give it an accessible name?
Add aria-label="Search" to the button
Add role="img" to the button
Add title to the SVG's parent div
Add tabindex="-1" to the button
Screen readers announce the accessible name. aria-label supplies one when there is no visible text.
A developer uses <div role="button"> instead of a native button. What must they also add?
tabindex="0" and handlers for the Enter and Space keys
aria-hidden="true" and a click handler on the div
type="button" and a name attribute so it submits forms
Nothing, the role adds full native button behavior
ARIA roles change only what assistive tech announces, not behavior. Focus and keyboard support must be implemented manually.
What does aria-hidden="true" do to an element?
Hides it from assistive tech while it stays visible
Hides it visually and from assistive tech at once
Prevents it from receiving mouse clicks or taps
Removes it from the DOM entirely after the page loads
aria-hidden removes the element from the accessibility tree only. Do not put it on focusable elements, or keyboard users reach invisible controls.
What alt value should a purely decorative image have?
An empty alt attribute, alt=""
A descriptive alt="decorative image"
The image's file name as alt text
No alt attribute on the img at all
An empty alt tells screen readers to skip the image. Leaving alt out entirely may make them read the file name.
A status message is inserted into the page after a form saves. Which attribute lets screen readers announce it politely?
aria-live="polite" on its container
aria-label="polite" on the message
role="presentation" on the container
tabindex="0" on the message
Live regions announce content changes. polite waits until the user is idle; assertive interrupts.

A form has <input type="email" required>. How can you turn off the browser's built-in validation for the whole form?
Add the novalidate attribute to the <form>

Change required to optional
Set autocomplete="off" on the <form>
novalidate on the form, or formnovalidate on a submit button, skips constraint validation on submit.

Add for="email" to the label

Add label="email" to the input

The pattern must match the entire value, as if wrapped in ^(?:...)$. Partial matches inside a longer string fail.
What happens when you click a <button> with no type attribute inside a <form>?
It submits the form
It does nothing by default
It resets all form fields
It only focuses the first input
The default button type inside a form is submit. Use type="button" for buttons that should not submit.

Cookies are sent with requests to their domain; localStorage is not
localStorage is sent with every request; cookies stay in the browser
Cookies can store far more data per domain than localStorage can
localStorage is cleared automatically when the browser tab is closed
Cookies travel in request headers, which suits sessions. localStorage stays in the browser and persists until it is cleared; sessionStorage ends with the tab.
A session cookie is set with the HttpOnly flag. What does that change?
JavaScript cannot read it through document.cookie
It is sent only over plain HTTP connections, not over HTTPS
It is deleted whenever any page on the site reloads
It can be read by scripts on any other website
HttpOnly hides the cookie from scripts, which limits damage from XSS. Secure restricts it to HTTPS.
After localStorage.setItem("n", 5), what does typeof localStorage.getItem("n") return?
"string"
"number"
"object"
"undefined"
Web Storage stores only strings, so 5 becomes "5". Use JSON.stringify and JSON.parse for structured data.
Which meta tag makes a page lay out at the device width on phones?

<meta name="mobile" content="responsive, device-width">
<meta http-equiv="width" content="device-width, scale=1">
<meta name="screen" content="fit-device, initial-zoom=1">
Without it, mobile browsers render at a wide virtual viewport (often 980px) and zoom out.
What is <meta name="description" content="..."> mainly used for?
A page summary that search engines may show in results
The tooltip shown when hovering the browser tab
Text read aloud by screen readers on load
The default alt text for images on the page
Search engines may use the description as the snippet under the title. It does not directly control ranking.
What happens if a page omits <!DOCTYPE html> at the top?
The browser renders it in quirks mode
The browser refuses to render the page
The page is parsed as XML instead
Only inline scripts are disabled
Without a doctype, browsers emulate old, non-standard layout behavior. <!DOCTYPE html> triggers standards mode.

25px
Adjacent vertical margins of blocks in normal flow collapse into the larger of the two. This does not happen in flex or grid layouts.

The vertical axis
The horizontal axis
Both axes equally
Neither axis, it is ignored

What does flex: 1 expand to on a flex item?
flex-grow: 1, flex-shrink: 1, flex-basis: 0%
flex-grow: 1, flex-shrink: 0, flex-basis: auto
flex-grow: 0, flex-shrink: 1, flex-basis: 1px
flex-grow: 1 with the other values unchanged
With a zero basis, items with flex: 1 share all space equally regardless of their content size.
Which CSS centers a single child both horizontally and vertically in its parent?
display: flex; justify-content: center; align-items: center
display: flex; text-align: center; vertical-align: middle
display: block; margin: auto; align-content: center
display: inline; justify-items: center; float: center
In a flex row, justify-content centers on the main (horizontal) axis and align-items centers on the cross (vertical) axis.
A flex row has many fixed-width items that overflow the container instead of moving to a new line. What fixes it?
flex-wrap: wrap on the container
flex-direction: row-reverse
align-items: stretch on the container
order: 1 on every flex item
Flex containers default to flex-wrap: nowrap, which forces all items onto one line.
What does grid-template-columns: repeat(3, 1fr) create?
Three columns that share the free space equally
Three rows of equal height that share the free space
One column that is 3fr wide in total
Three columns that are each 1px wide
repeat(3, 1fr) is shorthand for 1fr 1fr 1fr; the fr unit divides the remaining space in the grid container.
In a grid with explicit columns, which rule makes an item span all of them?
grid-column: 1 / -1
grid-column: span all
grid-column: 0 / 100%
grid-column: full
Line -1 is the last explicit grid line, so 1 / -1 stretches from the first line to the last.
Which grid-template-columns value creates as many columns of at least 200px as fit, stretching to fill the row?
repeat(auto-fill, minmax(200px, 1fr))
repeat(200px, minmax(auto, 1fr))
minmax(200px, repeat(auto-fill, 1fr))
repeat(auto-fill, 200px 1fr)
auto-fill (or auto-fit) creates as many tracks as fit, and minmax keeps each column between 200px and an equal share of the space.
An element has position: absolute; top: 0; right: 0. What is it positioned relative to?
The nearest ancestor that is not position: static
Its direct parent element, in every case
The browser viewport, in every case
Its own original place in the normal flow
Absolute positioning uses the nearest positioned ancestor as its containing block; if none exists, the initial containing block.
An element has position: sticky but does not stick, and its CSS sets no top, bottom, left or right. What fixes it?
Add an offset such as top: 0
Add z-index: 9999 to it
Change display to inline
Add float: left to the element
Sticky positioning needs a threshold offset. An ancestor with overflow: hidden can also stop it from working.
A position: fixed element sits inside a parent that has transform: translateX(0). What is it positioned relative to?
The transformed parent, not the viewport
The viewport, since transforms are ignored
The document root html element
The nearest scroll container
A transform, filter or perspective on an ancestor creates a containing block for fixed descendants, a common cause of broken modals.
Which selector wins: #header a or .menu .link a, if both set color on the same link?
#header a
.menu .link a
The later rule
Browser default
Specificity compares IDs first: #header a is (1,0,1) and .menu .link a is (0,2,1). One ID beats any number of classes.
A stylesheet has p { color: red !important; } and the element has style="color: blue". Which color shows?
Red
Blue
Purple
Black
Important declarations from author stylesheets beat normal declarations, including inline styles without !important.
What is the specificity of :where(#main .card) p?
(0,0,1), because :where() adds no specificity
(1,1,1), because every part is counted
(1,0,1), because only the ID is counted
(0,1,1), because :where() counts only the class
:where() always has zero specificity, which makes it useful for easy-to-override defaults. :is() takes its most specific argument.
What does padding: var(--gap, 8px) use when --gap is not defined anywhere?
8px
auto
inherit
The second argument of var() is a fallback used when the custom property is not defined.
Which JavaScript sets the CSS variable --accent to red on an element el?
el.style.setProperty("--accent", "red")
el.style["--accent"] = "red"
el.setAttribute("--accent", "red")
el.css.var("--accent", "red")
Custom properties are set with setProperty. They inherit, so children using var(--accent) update too.
In a mobile-first stylesheet, when does @media (min-width: 768px) { ... } apply?
At viewport widths of 768px and wider
At viewport widths below 768px
Only at a width of exactly 768px
Only on devices that report a tablet type
min-width queries add styles as the screen grows, which is the mobile-first approach. max-width does the opposite.
The root font-size is 16px and a parent has font-size: 20px. How wide is a child with width: 2rem?
32px
40px
20px
36px
rem is relative to the root (html) font size, so 2rem is 32px. 2em would use the parent's 20px and give 40px.
tailwind-css: With Tailwind's default spacing scale, how much padding does the class p-4 add?
1rem (16px) on all sides
4px on all sides
4rem on all sides
1rem on the top only
Each spacing step is 0.25rem by default, so 4 equals 1rem, which is 16px at the default root font size.
What does the class combination flex items-center justify-between do?
Makes a flex row, centers items vertically, spreads them apart
Makes a grid, centers every item in its cell, adds gaps between them
Centers the text and adds equal space between the words
Makes a column with all items packed tightly at the top
items-center sets align-items: center on the cross axis and justify-between sets justify-content: space-between on the main axis.
In Tailwind, what does class="hidden md:block" do?
Hidden on small screens, block from md up
Shown on small screens, hidden from md up
Hidden only at exactly the md width
Hidden until the user hovers over it
Tailwind is mobile-first: unprefixed utilities apply at all sizes, and md: applies at the md min-width and above.
With Tailwind's default breakpoints, from what viewport width do lg: utilities apply?
768px
992px
The defaults are sm 640px, md 768px, lg 1024px, xl 1280px and 2xl 1536px, each as a min-width.
In Tailwind v3.2 or later, which class hides an element only below the md breakpoint?
max-md:hidden
sm:hidden
md:hidden
below-md:hidden
max-* variants apply below a breakpoint. md:hidden hides from 768px up, and sm:hidden hides from 640px up.
In Tailwind v3, darkMode is set to "class" in the config. When do dark: utilities apply?
When an ancestor such as html has the class dark
Whenever the OS prefers a dark color scheme
After the user calls a Tailwind JS API
Only between sunset and sunrise
Class strategy lets you toggle dark mode manually by adding or removing the dark class, usually on the html element.
In Tailwind v3, if darkMode is not set in the config, what do dark: utilities respond to?
The prefers-color-scheme media feature
A dark class on the html element
A data-theme attribute on the body
A cookie named theme set by the page
The v3 default strategy is media, which follows the operating system setting. Switching to class or selector enables manual toggling.
In Tailwind v4, how do you make dark: utilities depend on a .dark class instead of the OS setting?
@custom-variant dark (&:where(.dark, .dark *)); in your CSS
darkMode: "class" set inside the tailwind.config.js file only
Adding the dark class to every element on the page
@apply dark; at the very top of your main CSS file
Tailwind v4 moved configuration into CSS. Overriding the dark variant with @custom-variant switches it to a class selector.
Which Tailwind class sets top to exactly 117px, a value not in the default scale?
top-[117px]
top-117
top-(117px)
top:117px
Square brackets create an arbitrary value, generating a one-off utility such as top: 117px.
How do you write an arbitrary grid with columns 1fr and 2fr as a single Tailwind class?
grid-cols-[1fr_2fr]
grid-cols-[1fr 2fr]
grid-cols-1fr-2fr
grid-cols-(1fr,2fr)
Class names cannot contain spaces, so Tailwind converts underscores in arbitrary values into spaces.
Which class sets a one-off background color of #1da1f2?
bg-[#1da1f2]
bg-#1da1f2
bg-color-1da1f2
background-[#1da1f2]
Arbitrary values work with color utilities too; Tailwind generates background-color: #1da1f2.
What does .btn { @apply px-4 py-2 rounded; } do in a Tailwind CSS file?
Copies those utilities' declarations into the .btn rule
Adds the classes to every button element in HTML
Creates three separate classes named btn
Links .btn to the utilities at runtime in JS
@apply inlines the CSS of existing utilities at build time, so .btn gets padding and border-radius declarations.
Which statement about @apply in Tailwind is accurate?
It accepts variants such as hover:bg-blue-600
It runs in the browser on each page load
It works only inside HTML style attributes
It cannot be used in plain .css files
@apply supports variants, so hover and responsive styles can be applied in custom CSS. The Tailwind docs recommend using it sparingly.
In Tailwind v3, classes used in src/components/Card.tsx get no styles in production. What is the likely cause?
The file is not matched by the content paths in the config
Tailwind ignores .tsx files unless a JSX plugin is installed first
Production builds strip out all custom class names
Card.tsx is missing an @tailwind import at the top
Tailwind v3 generates CSS only for class names found in the files listed in content. Files outside those globs are not scanned.

extend keeps the defaults; theme.colors replaces them
theme.colors keeps the defaults; extend replaces them
extend applies its colors only in dark mode

Add a brand key to a colors.json file in the project root
Run npx tailwind add-color brand in the terminal
Write a .bg-brand rule in a <style> tag in the HTML
In v4, theme variables live in CSS. A --color-* variable inside @theme generates the matching color utilities.
In React, className={"text-" + color + "-500"} gives no styles. Why?
Tailwind only finds complete class names in source text
Tailwind does not support class names inside React components
Dynamic classes need the !important modifier to apply
The default color scale stops at 400 for text colors
Tailwind scans files as plain text and never runs your code. Map values to full strings, such as { red: "text-red-500" }.

Only classes found in your files are generated
Every possible class ships to the browser
CSS is generated in the browser at runtime
Responsive variants must be enabled one by one

Add group to the parent and group-hover:text-white to the child
Add hover:children to the parent and text-white to the child
Add parent-hover:text-white to the child and nothing to the parent
Add peer to the child and hover:peer to the parent element

hidden
invisible
opacity-0

A geometry and a material
A texture and a light
A camera and a scene
A vertex shader and a renderer
Geometry defines the shape (vertices), and material defines how its surface looks when rendered.

The mesh is not drawn
It is drawn at the origin
Three.js adds it automatically
The renderer throws an error
The renderer only draws objects that are part of the scene graph passed to render().
In new THREE.PerspectiveCamera(75, w / h, 0.1, 1000), what does 75 mean?
The vertical field of view, in degrees
The horizontal field of view, in radians
The camera's distance from the origin
The maximum frames per second
The arguments are fov (vertical, in degrees), aspect ratio, near plane and far plane.
After the browser window is resized, which steps keep a Three.js perspective view undistorted?
Set camera.aspect, call updateProjectionMatrix(), resize renderer
Call scene.resize() and then renderer.reset() on each resize
Recreate the scene and every mesh from scratch on each resize
Set camera.fov to the new window width on each resize event
Changing the aspect alone does nothing until the projection matrix is recomputed; renderer.setSize updates the canvas.

OrthographicCamera
PerspectiveCamera
CubeCamera
StereoCamera
An orthographic projection has no perspective foreshortening, so object size does not depend on distance from the camera.

Move the camera back, for example camera.position.z = 5
Shrink the cube, for example cube.scale.set(0, 0, 0)
Clear the canvas, for example renderer.clear() each frame
Turn the camera, for example camera.rotation.x = Math.PI
Both start at (0, 0, 0), so the camera sits inside the cube. The camera looks down the negative Z axis by default.
After creating new THREE.WebGLRenderer(), what must you do for its output to appear on the page?
Append renderer.domElement to the document
Call renderer.mount("#app")
Set renderer.visible = true
Nothing, it draws on the body automatically
renderer.domElement is a canvas element. You append it yourself, or pass an existing canvas in the constructor options.
A Three.js scene looks blurry on high-DPI phone screens. Which renderer call helps?
renderer.setPixelRatio(window.devicePixelRatio)
renderer.setClearColor(window.devicePixelRatio)
renderer.setSize(window.devicePixelRatio)
renderer.toneMapping = window.devicePixelRatio
This renders at the device's real pixel density. Many apps cap it at 2 to limit GPU cost.
A mesh with MeshStandardMaterial renders completely black. What is the most likely cause?
The scene has no lights
The material has no texture
The camera is orthographic
The renderer has antialias enabled
MeshStandardMaterial is physically based and needs light. MeshBasicMaterial ignores lighting and would show its color.
How does RawShaderMaterial differ from ShaderMaterial in Three.js?
It does not prepend built-in uniforms and attributes
It can only sample textures, not use plain colors
It compiles and runs its shaders on the CPU instead of the GPU
It cannot receive any custom uniforms from JavaScript
ShaderMaterial injects definitions such as projectionMatrix and position for you; with RawShaderMaterial you declare everything yourself.
A material has opacity: 0.5, but the mesh still looks fully opaque. What is missing?
transparent: true on the material
alpha: 0.5 on the geometry
visible: false on the mesh
depthTest: true on the camera
Three.js only uses opacity when transparent is enabled, which also changes how the object is sorted and blended.
Which Three.js light lights all objects equally from no direction and casts no shadows?
AmbientLight
DirectionalLight
SpotLight
PointLight
AmbientLight adds a flat amount of light everywhere. Because it has no direction, it cannot cast shadows.
Which Three.js light models sunlight, with parallel rays coming from one direction?
DirectionalLight
PointLight
HemisphereLight
RectAreaLight
DirectionalLight behaves as if infinitely far away. PointLight spreads in all directions from a single point.
Lights and meshes have castShadow set, but no shadows appear. Which renderer setting is required?
renderer.shadowMap.enabled = true
renderer.shadows.enabled = "on"
renderer.castShadow = true
renderer.autoClear = false
Shadow mapping is off by default on the renderer. Receiving meshes also need receiveShadow = true.
mesh.rotation.y += 0.01 runs every frame, and the cube spins twice as fast on a 120 Hz screen. Which fix fits?
Scale the step by the time since the last frame
Call requestAnimationFrame twice per frame
Set renderer.fps = 60 before the loop starts
Use degrees instead of radians for the rotation
Frame-based steps depend on refresh rate. Multiplying a per-second speed by elapsed time, for example from THREE.Clock's getDelta(), keeps motion consistent.
Why might you use renderer.setAnimationLoop(fn) instead of calling requestAnimationFrame yourself?
It also works in WebXR sessions
It renders on a background thread
It caps every scene at 30 frames per second
It removes the need to call render()
WebXR uses the headset's own frame loop, which setAnimationLoop handles. You still call renderer.render inside fn.
After GLTFLoader loads a model, which object do you usually add to the scene?
gltf.scene
gltf.mesh
gltf.root
gltf.geometry
The loader passes a result object; gltf.scene holds the loaded hierarchy, and gltf.animations holds the animation clips.
GLTFLoader fails on a glTF file compressed with Draco. What is needed?
A DRACOLoader passed to loader.setDRACOLoader()
A TextureLoader passed to loader.setPath() before loading
Setting renderer.compressed = true before loading
Converting the file to OBJ format first
Draco-compressed geometry must be decoded by DRACOLoader, which needs the decoder files hosted at a path you set.
A loaded glTF has animations. Which approach plays the first clip?
Use an AnimationMixer, play its clipAction, update it each frame
Call gltf.animations[0].start() once, right after the model loads
Set gltf.scene.animate = true and the loader plays it
Call renderer.play(gltf.animations) inside the render loop
The mixer drives animation actions. mixer.update(delta) must run in the render loop to advance time.
webgl: How often does a vertex shader run?
Once for each vertex in the draw call
Once for each pixel on the whole canvas
Once per frame for the whole scene
Once when the program is linked
The vertex shader processes every vertex and must set gl_Position, the vertex position in clip space.
What is the main job of a fragment shader?
Computing the color of each fragment
Placing each vertex in clip space
Uploading vertex data to the GPU
Choosing which triangles to draw
Fragment shaders output a color per fragment, gl_FragColor in GLSL ES 1.00 or an out variable in GLSL ES 3.00.
In a WebGL 1 shader (GLSL ES 1.00), what happens with the line float x = 1; ?
A compile error: no implicit int to float
x becomes 1.0, with a compiler warning
x silently becomes 0.0 at runtime
x is treated as an int from then on
GLSL ES 1.00 has no implicit type conversions. Write 1.0 instead.
A WebGL 1 fragment shader fails with a precision error. Which line usually fixes it?
precision mediump float;
#version 100 float;
uniform float precision;
#define FLOAT_PRECISION
Fragment shaders in GLSL ES 1.00 have no default float precision, so you must declare one. Vertex shaders default to highp.
In GLSL, given vec4 v = vec4(1.0, 2.0, 3.0, 4.0), what is v.zyx?
A compile error
Swizzling picks components in any order: z is 3.0, y is 2.0 and x is 1.0.
How does a WebGL 1 vertex shader pass a per-vertex color to the fragment shader?
Through a varying, interpolated across the triangle
Through a uniform that is set inside the vertex shader
Through gl_FragColor written in the vertex shader
Through a texture that the vertex shader writes to
varying values (in and out in GLSL ES 3.00) are written per vertex and interpolated for each fragment.
A WebGL 2 shader uses in and out variables but fails to compile. What is likely missing?
#version 300 es as the very first line
precision highp int; at the end
#extension WEBGL2 : enable
A main2() function instead of main()
Without the version directive, the shader is compiled as GLSL ES 1.00, which has no in and out qualifiers. Nothing may come before it.
Which call uploads vertex positions into the currently bound WebGL buffer?
gl.bufferData(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER, new Float32Array(data), gl.STATIC_DRAW)
gl.uniform3fv(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER, new Float32Array(data), gl.STATIC_DRAW)
gl.vertexAttrib(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER, new Float32Array(data), gl.STATIC_DRAW)
gl.texImage2D(gl.ARRAY_BUFFER, new Float32Array(data), gl.STATIC_DRAW)
bufferData copies typed array data into the buffer bound to the target. STATIC_DRAW hints that it will not change often.
In gl.vertexAttribPointer(loc, 2, gl.FLOAT, false, 0, 0), what does the 2 mean?
Each vertex reads two components, such as x and y
The buffer contains two vertices in total
The attribute is stored at shader location number 2
The data is read every second byte
The size argument is the number of components per vertex (1 to 4). The attribute location is the first argument.
Every vertex appears at the same spot even though the buffer holds correct data. Which call is likely missing?
gl.enableVertexAttribArray(loc)
gl.enable(gl.DEPTH_TEST)
gl.vertexAttribDivisor(loc, 0)
gl.linkProgram(program)
A disabled attribute uses one constant value for every vertex instead of reading from the buffer.
An interleaved buffer stores x, y, z then r, g, b per vertex as 32-bit floats. What are the stride and color offset in bytes?
Stride 24, color offset 12
Stride 6, color offset 3
Stride 24, color offset 3
Stride 12, color offset 24
Each float is 4 bytes: 6 floats per vertex give a 24-byte stride, and colors start after 3 floats, at byte 12.
To reuse shared vertices across triangles with an index list, which buffer target and draw call do you use?
gl.ELEMENT_ARRAY_BUFFER with gl.drawElements
gl.ARRAY_BUFFER with gl.drawArrays and an offset
gl.INDEX_BUFFER with gl.drawIndexed
gl.UNIFORM_BUFFER with gl.drawRange
Indices live in an element array buffer and drawElements reads them to assemble primitives from shared vertices.
Which order matches the WebGL rendering pipeline?
Vertex shader, rasterization, fragment shader, depth test and blending
Fragment shader, vertex shader, rasterization, depth test and blending
Rasterization, vertex shader, depth test and blending, fragment shader
Depth test and blending, vertex shader, fragment shader, rasterization
Vertices are transformed first, triangles are rasterized into fragments, fragments are shaded, then per-fragment tests and blending write pixels.
After the perspective divide, what range of x and y is visible in WebGL?
-1 to 1
0 to 1
0 to canvas width
Normalized device coordinates span -1 to 1 on each axis; the viewport transform maps them to canvas pixels.
Objects drawn later always appear on top, even when they are farther away. Which call fixes this?

gl.enable(gl.BLEND)
gl.enable(gl.CULL_FACE)
gl.disable(gl.SCISSOR_TEST)

The value is queued until the program is next made current
The value applies to every linked program
The value is stored in the location for later
Uniform setters affect the program currently in use. With none, WebGL reports INVALID_OPERATION and nothing is set.
How does a uniform differ from an attribute in WebGL?
A uniform has one value for the whole draw call
A uniform changes for each vertex
A uniform can only be used in vertex shaders
A uniform is stored in an array buffer
Attributes supply per-vertex data from buffers; uniforms, such as a time value or matrix, are constant across a draw call.

false
true
Either value
The matrix count

model
projection
view
All at once
With column vectors, the matrix closest to the vector applies first: model to world space, then view, then projection.
After resizing a WebGL canvas to new pixel dimensions, why is the image squashed into a corner?

The shaders must be recompiled after a resize
The vertex buffers were cleared by the resize
The canvas lost its WebGL context

As one bundle rebuilt on every change
As a minified production build
As a Web Worker loaded into the page

vite.config.js under the entry key

As @public/logo.png

React DevTools saving state between edits

Only the CSS is updated

They run only during the production build step
They must be compiled to native code before use

Runs the plugin before Vite core plugins
Runs the plugin before the dev server starts
Makes the plugin required for every build
Runs the plugin only in production

Set enforce: "build" on the plugin

Only import.meta.env.VITE_API_URL

Env variables only work inside .vue or .jsx files

You change VITE_API_URL in .env after running vite build and redeploy the same dist. What does the app use?
The old value, inlined at build time
The new value, read at page load
undefined, since the file changed
The value from the user's browser

Serving the built dist folder locally to check it

Starting the dev server with HMR on a free port
Printing the bundle size report for each chunk

Excludes Chart from the production build output
Loads Chart synchronously during app startup

Empties the output directory before each build

Deletes unused npm packages from node_modules
Runs Prettier on the output files after each build

So webpack reads its source files from that folder
So the dev server stores its build cache there

A rule has use: ["style-loader", "css-loader"]. In what order do the loaders run?
css-loader first, then style-loader
style-loader first, then css-loader
Both at once, in parallel threads
In alphabetical order of loader name

To skip transpiling dependencies and speed up the build
Because Babel cannot read any files inside node_modules folders
To remove dependencies from the final bundle
To force dependencies to load from a public CDN

What does HtmlWebpackPlugin do?
Generates an HTML file with script tags for the bundles
Converts HTML templates into JavaScript modules at build time
Minifies the HTML of every page on the server
Checks the generated HTML for accessibility errors

In a production build, which change extracts CSS into separate .css files instead of injecting style tags?
Use MiniCssExtractPlugin's loader, not style-loader
Add css-loader twice to the same rule for .css files
Set output.css to true in the webpack config
Use type asset/inline for all .css files
MiniCssExtractPlugin emits CSS files that browsers can cache and load in parallel with JS.
new webpack.DefinePlugin({ API_URL: "https://api.example.com" }) causes a syntax error. What fixes it?
Wrap the value in JSON.stringify(...)
Move it into the output section
Use a template string as the key
Add a loader for .env files

How do loaders differ from plugins in webpack?
Loaders transform files; plugins hook into the build
Loaders run after the build finishes, plugins run before it starts
Plugins only handle CSS, loaders only handle JS

Loaders convert individual files (TS, CSS, images) into modules. Plugins tap compiler hooks for tasks like generating HTML or optimizing output.
What does import("./chart.js") inside a function do in a webpack build?
Creates a separate chunk loaded when the import runs
Inlines chart.js into the entry bundle
Throws an error, since webpack forbids dynamic imports
Loads chart.js from npm at runtime over the network

Which optimization setting splits shared vendor code out of both initial and async chunks?
optimization.splitChunks: { chunks: "all" }
optimization.minimize: { chunks: "all" }
output.chunkFilename: { chunks: "vendor" }
resolve.splitChunks: { chunks: "all" }

What does import(/* webpackChunkName: "chart" */ "./chart") change?
The name used for the emitted chunk
The order in which chunks are loaded
The module's export names
Whether the chunk is minified
The magic comment gives the chunk a readable name (used for [name]) instead of a numeric id.
Why does tree shaking work better with import and export than with require?
ES imports are static, so unused exports are found at build time
require calls are blocked by webpack in production mode
import statements execute much faster than require calls in Node.js
Webpack cannot include require calls in a bundle at all
Static import and export structure lets webpack mark unused exports, which the minifier removes in production mode.
After adding "sideEffects": false to package.json, styles from import "./styles.css" disappear. What fixes it?
Set "sideEffects": ["*.css"]
Remove css-loader from the config
Set mode to development
Rename the file to styles.module.js

A single-page app on webpack-dev-server shows 404 when refreshing /settings. Which option fixes it?
devServer.historyApiFallback: true
devServer.liveReload: true
output.publicPath: "/settings"
devServer.compress: true
historyApiFallback serves index.html for unknown paths, so the client-side router can handle the route.
During development, how do you forward /api requests from webpack-dev-server to a backend on port 4000 to avoid CORS?
Configure devServer.proxy for /api to http://localhost:4000
Set output.publicPath to http://localhost:4000/api for all requests
Set devServer.port to 4000 so both share one port
Use DefinePlugin to rewrite /api to localhost:4000
The dev server proxies matching requests, so the browser sees one origin and no CORS preflight is needed.
In webpack 5, what does a rule with type: "asset/resource" do for a .png import?
Emits the file to the output and exports its URL
Inlines the file into the bundle as a base64 data URI
Exports the file contents as a raw string
Ignores the file entirely during the build

Which webpack 5 asset module type exports a file's raw contents as a string?
asset/source
asset/resource
asset/inline
asset/url
asset/source replaces raw-loader and is handy for importing text files, such as GLSL shaders.
